timeToCredentials.basis: Our estimate: creating a developer app with an existing LinkedIn account and Page is instant account registration. The docs describe no wait, so we allow time to set up a Page and fill in the app form.

timeToProduction.basis: One third-party developer reported a review of about two weeks, ending in a rejection. Official sources state no review wait time. Production access needs two reviews (Development tier, then Standard tier with a screen recording and test credentials), and a rejected app cannot reapply: a new app and a new Development tier request are needed. Treat this range as a lower bound.

humanEffortHours.basis: Our estimate (no primary source gives hours): setting up the Page and app, a privacy policy, organization proof and a business email, the access form, the Standard tier screen recording and test credentials, and recreating the app if it is rejected.

verdict.summary: Member-level posting works with open scopes right after you create an app. Posting as a Page or organization needs w_organization_social, which is gated behind a manual product review. That review likely takes weeks and requires proof of a legally registered organization.
verdict.biggestLaunchRisk: The product review for w_organization_social can be rejected on identity vetting. One developer reported a rejection because their organizational website did not prove a legally registered, active entity.

managedCovers.text: Composio's managed-auth directory lists LinkedIn as having Composio-managed OAuth. That would let you prototype without registering your own LinkedIn app.

youNeedOwnWhen.text: The sources do not say which scopes the Composio-managed LinkedIn app covers. If you need w_organization_social to post as a Page for your own customers, confirm that scope is available. Otherwise plan to register your own app and pass LinkedIn's review.

You need your own app if you want your own branding, your own Client ID and Secret, and your own LinkedIn approval status for the Page or organization posting product. LinkedIn grants product access per app.

requirements.text: A LinkedIn member account in good standing, and agreement to the LinkedIn API Terms of Use.
If building for a company, you must have full legal authority to register an app for that entity and bind it to the Terms.
A LinkedIn Page associated with the app, and a super admin of that Page must verify the app (the super admin has 30 days to approve the association request).
A review of LinkedIn's API and data restrictions to confirm the use case is supported.
An HTTPS redirect (callback) URL added under the app's Auth tab.

Community Management APIs are only available to registered legal organizations for commercial use cases. LinkedIn reviews the approved use case, a verified business email (personal addresses fail), the verified organization, its verified website and domain, and a Page-verified app. Share the legal name, registered address, website and privacy policy. One developer reported that a GitHub Pages docs site was not accepted (blog only).

A privacy policy is required (the access request asks for it and Standard tier review checks for a valid one). Documentation of posting behavior and data use is what one developer wrote; LinkedIn does not list it as a requirement.

scopesAndNuances.text: Open permissions available to all apps are profile and email (Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect) and w_member_social (Share on LinkedIn), all via 3-legged OAuth and added self-service on the Products tab. Older pages still name r_liteprofile and r_emailaddress.

Everything beyond the open set needs LinkedIn approval (documented). Requesting an unapproved scope gives a 403 'Not enough permissions' error (reported by a third-party blog; LinkedIn's OAuth page documents a 401 'Invalid scope' for the authorization endpoint).

Posting to a Page needs w_organization_social. LinkedIn's docs list it under the Community Management API (and Advertising API) products, which require an access request and review (Development tier, then Standard tier). 'Share on LinkedIn' only grants w_member_social. One developer's blog called the gate 'Share on LinkedIn'; the official docs do not.
Marketing APIs, including Community Management, require member (3-legged) authorization. 2-legged client credentials OAuth is not available for Marketing APIs.
2-legged OAuth is not available by default. A 401 'not allowed to create application tokens' error means contacting the LinkedIn Relationship Manager or Business Development team.
LinkedIn has a Self-Serve API Program with APIs available immediately on registration, and Vetted API Programs that need eligibility and additional terms.
Standard rate limits are not published. They appear per app in the Developer Portal Analytics tab after at least one call to an endpoint. A 429 is returned when limits are exceeded.

Token lifetimes: authorization codes last 30 minutes. Access tokens last 60 days (3-legged). Programmatic refresh tokens last 365 days but are only available to approved partners or apps where enabled; otherwise the member must re-authorize. 2-legged tokens last 30 minutes.
